title: Matched/missing skill chips are LLM-narrated, not from a deterministic CV↔JD matcher
expected: Per the journey DoD ('no skill appears that isn't in the CV'), matched/missing skills trace to a deterministic taxonomy matcher comparing extracted CV skills against JD skills, so a 'matched' skill cannot be invented.
got: job_fit.matching_skills / missing_skills are extracted directly from the Gemini job-fit JSON (LLM narration). The UI cross-checks each 'matched' chip against the CV evidenceTrace.skills only to decide whether to show a tooltip (whole-token match), so a matched skill not in the CV renders without a tooltip but is NOT hard-blocked. Only the independent ATS keyword-coverage layer is deterministic, and it supplements rather than gates the LLM lists.
evidence: pipeline/jobfit/pipeline.py:617-634 (_job_fit_from_payload reads matching_skills/missing_skills straight from the LLM payload)
pipeline/jobfit/pipeline.py:215-242 (independent ATS keyword coverage supplements, does not replace, the LLM lists)
l2_priority: Run a real engineer CV + the seeded ČS JD; adversarially verify every 'matched' chip is findable in the CV text. Any invented match is a senior-quality quality-gap (blocker if Eva would be embarrassed to show a director).
suggested_acceptance: Every skill in jobFit.matchingSkills is present in the candidate's extracted CV skills / evidence; matched chips with no CV evidence are suppressed or flagged, never shown as a confirmed match.

title: Keyless run halts the core analyze with no labelled deterministic fallback
expected: Per env.md a keyless run degrades gracefully and is marked (scope_note); structural L1 still applies.
got: The core Gemini analyze has no deterministic fallback — get_gemini_api_key() raises if no key, the analysis aborts, and no 'deterministic mode' label is emitted. Only the cheap post-Gemini add-ons (_softly) degrade. For Eva this just means an AI key is required; out-of-scope for quality findings keyless.
evidence: pipeline/jobfit/cli.py:67-78 (catches and emits an error event, no deterministic mode)
scope_note: Keyless analyze is out-of-scope for quality findings (env.md). Recorded as a structural note; AI keys must be present for L2 quality findings to be in scope.
suggested_acceptance: A keyless analyze returns a clear, user-facing 'AI key required' state rather than a generic failure; if a deterministic skeleton is ever produced it is explicitly labelled as such.

title: Salary is benchmark-anchored and cites its basis — clears Eva's 'no number from a hat' bar
expected: A salary number Eva can stake her name on, grounded in a band/benchmark not a free-floating LLM guess.
got: data/salary_benchmarks.json (real CZK monthly-gross role×seniority bands, sourced Platy.cz 2026 / Kitalent / expats.cz / Glassdoor+Levels) is loaded deterministically and role_band() is fed to Gemini as the PRIMARY anchor (adjust ~±20% only on stronger evidence, and cite the anchor in salary.rationale). The band is sanitized + plausibility-capped (350k/mo flags garbage). The UI surfaces gauge + confidence + rationale + salaryEvidence trace + a grounded marketEvidence panel with vetted source links.
evidence: app/_components/results/salary/SalaryTab.tsx:43,63,66-103 (basis, rationale, evidence trace, grounded market evidence)

title: Real JD is a hard gate for job-fit; independent ATS layer surfaces what the LLM missed
expected: Job-fit is against THIS role, not a generic rubric.
got: The real JD flows cli.py -> service.py -> gemini.py into the prompt and job_fit is populated only when a JD is supplied (else null). A keyword-coverage ATS pass harvests the JD keyword universe deterministically from the JD text (taxonomy skill_keyword_pool), surfacing a JD keyword the candidate or the LLM missed — with deterministic in-JD / in-CV counts in the UI.

title: Analysis runs as a navigation-surviving background task; meter charges only delivered, non-cached work
expected: A long Gemini+Python analysis shouldn't be lost on navigation, and shouldn't over-charge on failed/cached runs.
got: POST /api/analyze starts a background 'analyze' task tracked by the global Tasks indicator (survives navigation/refresh); the AI-candidate meter is debited only on a delivered, non-cached result (a failure/cancel/duplicate never charges).

title: Eval/skill narrative prose is LLM-authored; scores are grounded but the prose's evidence-traceability must be confirmed on a real submission
expected: An evaluation Eva can defend to an eng director: a rubric + the candidate's actual decisions/artifacts cited as evidence, not a bare score or a vibe verdict.
got: The SCORES are grounded in observed signal (probe outcomes, seed-engagement diff, DECISIONS-log presence, reflect/tooling) and confidence is the MIN of upstream signals — strong. BUT the human-readable strengths/concerns/summary and the analyze matched-skills are LLM-authored prose, not independently traceable line-by-line to artifacts. On paper this clears the bar; it cannot be fully certified until a real submission's eval prose is read. Carried forward as the L1-conditional major (shared root with EVA-CVJF-1).
l2_priority: Seed a published case + a real submission, run the eval, and read the EvalPanel: assert the strengths/concerns/summary cite the candidate's actual observed decisions (files touched, DECISIONS.md, which probe option they shipped) and read as evidence rather than a generic grade; confirm the follow-ups are specific to the submission.
suggested_acceptance: On a real submission, every eval claim in strengths/concerns is traceable to an observed artifact (probe outcome, seed-diff, DECISIONS entry, reflection); Eva can point to WHY the verdict concluded what it did from the candidate's own work.

title: Authoring requires a pre-saved JD; the need cannot be entered as free text
expected: From a concrete engineering NEED, generate a case quickly without designing a bespoke problem from scratch.
got: NeedForm requires a saved JD picked from the library (the JD body IS the need's title/stack/responsibilities). Only 1 JD is seeded locally, so to author a second role Eva must first detour to /?tab=library and write a JD. Defensible design (the JD is the authoritative need statement) but a flow dependency and a friction point if the role need exists only in her head.
evidence: app/features/sub_dev/NeedForm.tsx:53-90 (JD required, picker marked *, Run/Analyze disabled until a JD body loads)
app/features/sub_dev/DevTab.tsx:167-185 (buildNeed: title/jdText from the picked JD; stack/responsibilities deliberately empty)
data/kp.sqlite: jds=1 (only one JD to pick)
suggested_acceptance: Either a quick free-text need entry path exists, or the JD-required flow makes the 'save a JD first' step a one-click inline action from the Define-need form.

title: Eval-reading half is reachable but unpopulated — no seeded published case + submission
expected: Per env.md fixture #4/#5, a published dev case + a candidate submission so the dev workspace + eval have content to defend.
got: dev_cases=0, dev_postings=0, dev_submissions=0, dev_lifecycle=0 in data/kp.sqlite. The authoring + publish path is reachable and Eva can mint everything live, but to READ an evaluation she can defend she must first collect a submission — so the 'defensible eval' end of her job cannot be earned at L1. Tagged unreachable for the eval-reading sub-step; verdict defers to L2 after running the seed.
evidence: env.md fixtures table row 'Dev case + submission' (devcase/seed_materializer.py) not run
scope_note: Fixture gap, not a product defect. The surfaces are correct in code; they just have no data yet.
l2_priority: Run devcase/seed_materializer.py + publish a case + submit via the apply token, then confirm CaseDetail/EvalPanel render the evidence-backed verdict end to end.

title: Case generation is anchored to the real JD + real stack, seniority-scaled — not a generic template
expected: A case generated from the actual role, not the same fizzbuzz shape regardless of role.
got: design_role anchors the role identity to the real JD body (the authoritative need statement); design_case calibrates to the real stack, scales the timebox by seniority (junior 3h … lead 8h), forces the role's own vocabulary, and explicitly forbids a generic puzzle / a case in the codebase's domain when it differs from the role being hired.

title: The case's instrument is ambiguity + a mandated DECISIONS log assuming 100%-LLM code — probes AI collaboration, not algorithm recall
expected: A case that probes human-AI collaboration and real judgment, brief and AI-allowed, that a strong senior wouldn't refuse and a bot can't one-shot.
got: The design prompt assumes the candidate's code is 100% LLM-generated, so the instrument is 2-4 covert probes (ambiguity/legacy_trap/verification_trap/underspecified) each with a decisionSpace of defensible options, plus a mandated visible DECISIONS log. The case forces the submission to encode a choice; AI is allowed and observed, the timebox keeps it short.
evidence: pipeline/jobfit/devcase/design.py:62-66 (system prompt: assume LLM-generated, probe judgment)

title: Eval mints candidate-specific interview follow-ups anchored to observed decisions — scores are hypotheses the interview verifies
expected: A verdict Eva can defend to a director by pointing to WHY it concluded what it did from the candidate's own work ('obájím to čím?').
got: mint_followups turns the evaluation into 4-6 questions each anchored to one observed decision (which decisionSpace option they shipped, a silent assumption, an abandoned dead end), asking for the why / rejected alternative / counterfactual — with internal listenFor/redFlag notes. The panel states explicitly that scores are hypotheses and the follow-ups are what verify authorship live.

title: Degraded generations are flagged distinctly; probes never leak to the candidate
expected: Honest about strengths and gaps; AI use acknowledged not pretended-away; the candidate never sees the answer key.
got: A template-only interview scenario or skeleton-only seed gets its OWN audit action (not a success row) and an amber badge in CaseDetail, so Eva is never handed generic template probes silently. The candidate page renders only caseToMarkdown, which excludes probes by construction — no probe/answer-key leak.
